transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel constantly wound up and on edge, like I can’t relax even when I’m just at home with my family. My wife actually urged me to come in and talk to someone because I just can't seem to shake this tension anymore.
Would you say your primary struggle is persistent worry about many different areas of your life, or did these feelings start specifically after a stressful life event?

It’s really a mix of both. It started escalating about nine months ago when my wife went back to work and I took on a major cloud migration project, but now it has snowballed into constant, everyday worry about almost everything. I’m constantly stressing over my kids, my parents' health, work deadlines, and my marriage, and I just can't seem to shut it off.
Do you feel that your current level of worry is disproportionate to the actual events in your life, or is it primarily focused on managing the specific changes that happened nine months ago?

It definitely feels disproportionate now. While it started with those big changes nine months ago, it has spiraled to the point where simple, everyday things like planning dinner or a routine meeting feel like high-stakes crises. I get stuck in these endless "what-if" scenarios that I just can't seem to shut off.
Beyond the constant worrying, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, fatigue, or difficulty with sleep?

Yes, absolutely. I constantly feel like I've had three cups of coffee too many—my shoulders are tense up by my ears, my leg is always bouncing, and I'm too keyed up to wind down. On top of that, my sleep is a mess because I lie awake for hours replaying schedules and then wake up at 3 or 4 a.m. completely exhausted, so I never feel rested.
Beyond the physical tension and sleep issues, have you noticed that your mind often goes blank or that you have been feeling more irritable than usual lately?

Yes, both of those have been happening. I frequently lose my train of thought and go completely blank mid-sentence during meetings or conversations. I've also been much more irritable lately, snapping at my wife and withdrawing from the family because I'm just so overwhelmed.
